newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch CPB has no comment on leaked forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Dutch CPB has no comment on leaked forecasts.

text.p: The Dutch government's central planning bureau (CPB) on Monday declined to comment on a newspaper report which said the bureau had raised its forecast of Dutch GDP growth for 1998 to 3.75 percent from 3.25 percent.
"These are not official figures, so we cannot comment on them," a CPB official said in response to questions about a report in the Algemeen Dagblad newspaper.
The CPB is scheduled to publish an updated forecast for the Dutch economy in early July. It last published an official forecast in early April.

Algemeen Dagblad said the CPB had also raised its 1997 GDP growth forecast to 3.25 percent from 3.0 percent and calculated that faster growth would boost tax revenues by an extra two billion guilders in 1997 and an extra four billion in 1998.
The newspaper said the CPB now forecast that the Dutch public sector deficit would fall to 1.75 percent of GDP in 1998 while the public sector debt would fall to 71.4 percent of GDP.
